description: A sequencer shaped like a bead board: on each gate a marble drops one row and either stays in its column or moves one to the right, and the knob it lands on sets the output voltage

params.text: Sets the voltage sent out when the marble lands here, -4V to 6V; the lamp at its centre lights while the marble is on it
Sets the chance that an incoming gate is acted on at all, 0 to 1, starting at 1
Transposes every knob in the triangle by whole octaves, -3 to 3
Spreads the notes of the chosen scale over this many octaves before starting again at the lowest, 1 to 6

inputs.text: A voltage above 2V drops the marble one row; it has to fall below 0.1V before another will be taken
A voltage above 2V puts the marble back on the top knob and sets the probability knob back to 1
Sets the probability directly over 0 to 10V for 0 to 1, overriding the probability knob while patched and turning the knob to match
Picks the root note the triangle is filled from, over the hundredths of a volt that a keyboard's C4 to B4 produce
Picks the scale or arpeggio the triangle is filled from over 0 to 10V, in the order the Scale/Arp menu lists them

outputs.text: Carries the voltage of the knob the marble is on, held until the next gate is acted on
Carries a copy of the incoming gate, for as long as that gate is high, and nothing at all for a gate the probability setting threw away

notes: changing the root note, the scale, the direction, the transpose or the octaves overwrites all 55 knobs at once, so anything set by hand is lost the moment one of those changes
the marble starts on the top knob and drops one row per gate; after the tenth row it starts again at the top
a reset is a full initialise: besides moving the marble back to the top it puts the probability knob back to 1
the root note jack matches its voltage against eleven exact hundredths of a volt; anything between them is read as B, so a slewed source will not track it
menu: Root Note: C, C#/Db, D, D#/Eb, E, F, F#/Gb, G, G#/Ab, A, A#/Bb, B — picks the note the scale is built from when the triangle is filled
Scale/Arp — picks the scale or arpeggio the triangle is filled from, twelve scales followed by sixteen arpeggios
Scale Direction: Up, Down — chooses whether the triangle is filled from the lowest note of the scale upwards or from the highest downwards

inputs.0: high above 2V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.1: high above 2V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.2:
0 to 10V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads the probability knob; a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.3:
0 to 1V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads the Root Note menu.
inputs.4:
0 to 10V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads the Scale/Arp menu.
